newsitem.title: USA: Status of 14 Cubans who crossed to Florida uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Status of 14 Cubans who crossed to Florida uncertain.

text.p: Fourteen Cubans who sailed across to Florida awaited word on their future on Monday in what could be the first test of proposed changes to U.S. policy on illegal immigrants from the Communist-ruled island.
A spokesman for the U.S. Immigration & Naturalisation Service said they arrived in the Florida Keys near Key Largo by boat on Sunday after spending four or five days at sea.

The group included 10 adult men, two women, a 17-year-old boy and a 6-year-old girl. The minors were released to local community agencies, their parents were being held at the Krome Immigrant Processing Centre outside Miami and the rest of the group were in detention near Sarasota, Florida.
"That's where space was available," the INS spokesman said.

For three decades, virtually all Cubans arriving in the United States have been allowed to stay, regardless of whether they arrived legally or illegally, reflecting U.S. opposition to the government of Cuban President Fidel Castro.

In May 1995, Washington agreed to send back to Cuba illegal migrants who were intercepted at sea while trying to reach the United States. But the relatively few Cubans who reached the U.S. mainland still were allowed to remain.
Earlier this month, U.S. and Cuban officials said they had agreed to work toward an accord under which Washington would repatriate Cubans arriving illegally in the United States.
The INS spokesman in Miami said he had no indication of any policy shift that would change the way Sunday's arrivals would be treated. "It's business as usual," he said.
